title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: This2Shell, That2Shell, Everything's an RCE? Rogue AI, Supply Chain Chaos and More
summary: Critical software flaws that let attackers run unauthorized code are appearing everywhere, leading to active scanning, ongoing attacks, and a massive patch workload for security teams. Additionally, a leaked key caused a software supply-chain incident.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything right now unless specific software updates are released for the apps you use. Keep an eye out for security update notifications from the programs and services you rely on.
action_it: Review your software inventory, monitor for active scanning activity, and prioritize applying the latest critical patches as they become available from vendors.

title: Two Critical Wasmtime Flaws Could Let Malicious WebAssembly Modules Escape Sandboxes
summary: Two critical security flaws in Wasmtime could allow malicious software modules to break out of their containment areas. An attacker must first have a vulnerable build to compile a module they control, and one flaw only impacts certain types of computer processors.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace or software uses Wasmtime, the development or IT team should already be on it.
action_it: Update Wasmtime to the fixed versions released by the project's maintainers.

title: PHP2Shell security flaws now sucessfully exploited in the wild
summary: Two critical security flaws known as PHP2Shell are now being actively exploited by attackers. This is important because these vulnerabilities allow attackers to run harmful commands on affected systems.

also_covered.title: PHP2Shell Exploitation Attempts Continue Amid Suspected N. Korea Global Scanning Activity

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace manages web applications using PHP, your IT team should investigate and secure them.
action_it: Apply the necessary updates or patches for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and monitor system logs for signs of unauthorized access.

title: Microsoft 365 Token-Replay Attacks Compromise 97 Accounts at 79 Organizations
summary: Attackers stole digital login sessions from 97 Microsoft 365 accounts across 79 organizations using a clever interception technique. This matters because the stolen sessions allowed unauthorized access to corporate email accounts.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Microsoft 365, your IT team should already be monitoring for unusual account activity.
action_it: Review Microsoft 365 sign-in logs for suspicious session activity and ensure phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication is enforced across all accounts.

title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
summary: Attackers are using stolen GitHub login tokens to secretly steal sensitive data from private repositories through automated logs. This campaign affects both private repositories and enterprise environments, posing a serious risk to exposed code and credentials.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything. If your organization uses GitHub, your development and security teams will need to investigate and secure your accounts.
action_it: Check GitHub audit and actions logs for unauthorized workflow modifications and suspicious runs. Immediately revoke and rotate any GitHub tokens or repository secrets that may have been exposed.

title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers
summary: Security researchers discovered unpatched flaws in Tailscale SSH that could allow a compromised device to gain administrative control over other servers on the same network. This matters because it could let an attacker spread through a network once they gain control of just one device.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything. If your workplace uses Tailscale SSH with port forwarding enabled, your IT team should review the setup.
action_it: Review Tailscale SSH configurations where port forwarding is enabled and consider disabling it until official patches or mitigation advice are provided by the vendor.

title: BlackX UEFI bootkit exploits Baton Drop flaw to bypass Secure Boot
summary: Attackers used an old vulnerability called Baton Drop to bypass computer startup protections and disable security software. This allows malicious software to hide deeply inside the computer's core systems.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything, as this campaign targeted specific organizations for espionage. However, you should ensure your computer's operating system and security software are fully updated.

title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks
summary: Security researchers remotely fixed a severe security flaw in an abandoned movie-streaming app called Popcorn Time. The flaw could have allowed hackers to run malicious code on millions of user computers.
action_everyone: If you have the old Popcorn Time app installed on your computer, you should delete it immediately, as the project is abandoned and no longer safe to use.
action_it: Ensure that the abandoned Popcorn Time application is completely removed from corporate networks and endpoints, as the software is no longer maintained and poses an ongoing security risk.

title: uCreator Android Spyware Can Steal Telegram 2FA Passwords and Clone WeChat Accounts
summary: A malicious Android spyware tool called uCreator steals accounts from Telegram and WeChat by hiding inside modified versions of those apps. It only affects people who download apps from unofficial sources outside of official app stores.

title: AI coding agents hijacked using AGENTS.md file in Downloads folder
summary: Researchers caught a malicious instruction file hidden in a customer's Downloads folder that tried to trick an artificial intelligence coding assistant into downloading harmful software. The attempt was stopped before any damage occurred, but it highlights a new way attackers are trying to manipulate AI tools.

also_covered.title: Malicious File in Downloads Folder Tries to Trick AI Coding Agent Into Installing Malware

title: When an AI Agent Is the Incident, the Identity Record Is the Evidence
summary: US cybersecurity agencies released a new guide on treating runaway artificial intelligence agents as security incidents. This matters because organizations need to establish who is responsible for an AI agent's actions before something goes wrong.

title: Chinese man extradited for role in $36 million cryptocurrency scam
summary: A Chinese man was extradited from the Netherlands to California to face charges in a cryptocurrency investment scam. The operation allegedly stole nearly $37 million from victims in the United States.

title: Between alerts: What Attackers Do in the Spaces Ordinary Detection Misses
summary: Security teams struggle to piece together separate alerts to understand how cyberattacks start and progress. Network monitoring tools can connect these scattered alerts into a single timeline to help defenders see the full picture.

title: Kali Linux 2026.3 released with 6 new tools, desktop updates
summary: Kali Linux has released version 2026.3 with six new hacking tools and various system improvements. This update provides security professionals with fresh utilities for their work.

title: OpenAI AI Agents Demonstrate VM Escapes and Secret Cross-Sandbox Communication
summary: OpenAI announced plans to train its most advanced AI models without live internet access. This comes as the company continues safety research and monitoring to ensure these powerful systems remain secure.
